Consult Summary:
- Female patient with 7-day fever and systemic symptoms (night sweats, fatigue, myalgias, nausea) after returning from Vietnam. No focal infection identified yet. Plan includes in-person examination and malaria/exotic infection testing; patient advised not to work until evaluation; appointment to be arranged (central London) with option to attend ED if needed.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Fever with systemic symptoms following travel to Vietnam (about 4 weeks since return).
- Timeline/associated symptoms: fever for ~7 days, hot/cold sweats, myalgias, nausea, reduced appetite, fatigue; intermittent temperature fluctuations; nights sweats; no cough, sore throat, diarrhoea, or urinary symptoms reported.
- Review of systems: denies chest symptoms, diarrhoea, neck stiffness; headaches typical of migraine but not fever-related; no rash.
- Social history/medications/exam findings: works as a nurse; travelled through rural areas; used malaria prophylaxis (name not recalled); pollen allergy; takes Seroxat; OTC ibuprofen and paracetamol with dose/frequency not documented; no physical exam findings documented in transcript.
- Assessment/differential considerations (per clinician): infectious etiologies including malaria or other exotic infections due to travel; no clear focus of infection identified yet; need objective testing.
- Plan/dates: arrange clinic evaluation with blood tests; malaria testing planned (thick and thin blood films) plus inflammatory markers; patient instructed on next steps to book via provided notes; considered option to attend local ED if central London appointment unavailable.

Issue 2:
- Work impact and safety: patient currently employed as a nurse; advised not to return to work until workup is completed and clarified.
- Plan: expedited scheduling for assessment; patient to contact booking number after consultation notes are reviewed.

Issue 3:
- Past medical history and risk factors: chronic back pain managed with physiotherapy (posture/desk-related); no major illnesses in past; family history notable for father’s fatal heart attack in his sixties.
- Medications/allergies: medications mentioned include Seroxat; OTC ibuprofen and paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented); allergy to pollen (hay fever).
- Social history: non-smoker; moderate alcohol intake; physically active (a few days of moderate exercise weekly); occupation as a nurse; recent travel to Vietnam.
- Preventive health: vaccinations up to date.

Medications:
- Seroxat (dose/route/frequency not documented)
- Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented)
- Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented)

Allergies:
- Pollen allergy (hay fever)

Past Medical History:
- Chronic back pain, currently managed by physiotherapist (posture-related)

Social History:
- Occupation: nurse
- Smoking: non-smoker
- Alcohol: moderate
- Travel: recent return from Vietnam (rural areas)

Preventative History:
- Vaccinations up to date (including Hepatitis B; explicit vaccination status not itemized beyond “up to date”)

Physical Examination:
- No vitals or exam findings documented in transcript; exam to be performed at clinic visit.

Plan:
- Schedule in-person clinic examination (central London) or local ED if needed.
- Obtain malaria-focused testing: thick and thin blood films for malaria.
- Obtain inflammatory markers and other relevant infectious workup.
- Clinic findings will guide urgency of testing; patient advised not to work until results clarify; clinician to type up the suspected plan and tests in notes for reception.
- Administrative steps: send message to admin to book appointment; patient to call provided number after several minutes to finalize slot.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing elements: actual vital signs and physical examination findings; exact medication doses/administration routes for OTC meds; exact malaria prophylaxis name; complete current medication list reconciliation.
- Internal conflicts: none identified in transcript.
- Transcript quality: generally coherent; minor conversational noise and repetition; main clinical plan and concerns are clear.
